sentences.text: Tuarangisaurus is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur found in New Zealand and Argentina.
This marine reptile reached a total length of over 8 meters.
The preserved skull measured approximately 37.0 cm in length, while the estimated total skull length is 37.5 cm.
It is distinguished by a unique combination of traits, including an ectopterygoid with a long process directed backward and a large boss of bone underneath.
A stapes bone is present in the holotype, a feature previously thought to be absent in elasmosaurids.
A juvenile specimen attributed to Tuarangisaurus contained at least thirty gastroliths.
The only known species, Tuarangisaurus keyesi, was originally named by Wiffen and Moisley in 1985.
The holotype specimen was collected by amateur paleontologists on March 20, 1978, from the Maungataniwha Sandstone Member of the Tahora Formation.
In 2026, O'Gorman, Scasso, and Medina assigned an elasmosaurid specimen from the Lefipán Formation of Argentina to Tuarangisaurus keyesi.
Tuarangisaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Tuarangisaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
